section_summary: This section contains United States Embassy Tokyo monthly political reports (Reports Nos. 101, 102, and 103) and Department of State memoranda covering Japanese domestic affairs, international diplomacy, and economic conditions from February through April 1935. Major diplomatic subjects include foreign resistance to the newly enacted Manchukuo oil monopoly and Japanese Petroleum Industry Law, the successful conclusion and signing of the sale of the Chinese Eastern Railway to Manchukuo, the state visit of Manchukuo Emperor Kangte to Tokyo, and trade tensions with the United States and Latin America. Domestically, the reports record significant parliamentary friction over the 1935-36 national budget, reactionary terrorism such as the assault on Yomiuri Shimbun president Matsutaro Shoriki, and an intense ultra-nationalist campaign against Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's constitutional 'organ theory' of the Imperial institution.

subfiles.about: Monthly political report detailing Japanese diplomatic relations, domestic politics, reactionary activities, and economic and financial conditions during February 1935.
subfiles.summary: Reviews diplomatic conflicts surrounding the Manchukuo oil monopoly, discriminatory customs tariffs against American and British kerosene, and the mistreatment and arrest of American executives of the Corn Products Refining Corporation by Osaka police. Details bilateral negotiations concerning the sale of the Chinese Eastern Railway, the border settlement following the Jehol incident, and northern fisheries disputes with Soviet Russia. Analyzes internal political developments, including the War Department's national crisis pamphlet, right-wing attacks on Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's constitutional theories, Diet debates on rural relief and the budget, and the reactionary sword attack on Matsutaro Shoriki.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of February, 1935 (Report No. 101)

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum evaluating Embassy Tokyo's monthly political reporting and its utility to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Damaged minute sheet on the Embassy's monthly political report, noting its matters were already known to the Division.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum regarding Embassy Political Report

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on political, international, and economic conditions in Japan for March 1935, along with monthly lists of despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report No. 102 covering major diplomatic milestones in March 1935, notably the initialing and formal signing in Tokyo of the agreements transferring Soviet ownership of the Chinese Eastern Railway to Manchukuo, guaranteed by Japan. Covers the formal announcement that the Manchukuo oil monopoly would take effect on April 10, the rejection of British and American objections, the collapse of shipping negotiations with the Netherlands, and Japan's formal withdrawal from the League of Nations becoming effective on March 27. Reports on the close of the Diet session, the passage of the budget and special business profits tax, and the fierce reactionary agitation against Dr. Minobe and Privy Council President Baron Ikki over constitutional interpretations of the Imperial throne.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1251 Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of March, 1935 (Report No. 102)

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum critically reviewing the Embassy's April 1935 political report and recommending procedural changes in report preparation.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Memo says the April 1935 political report merely repeats earlier despatches and telegrams, and suggests changing how it is prepared.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum regarding Embassy's Political Report for April 1935

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on political, diplomatic, and economic developments in Japan for April 1935.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report No. 103 detailing the tour of the American Economic Mission headed by W. Cameron Forbes to Japan, China, and the Philippines, and rising Japanese protests against alleged American and Latin American campaigns to restrict Japanese cotton textile exports. Records the formal implementation of the Manchukuo oil sales monopoly on April 10, the breakdown of talks under the Petroleum Industry Law, and final American representations asserting Japan's ultimate responsibility for injuries to American oil interests. Highlights the official state visit of Manchukuo Emperor Kangte (Puyi) to Tokyo, negotiations regarding joint Japan-Manchukuo economic control, and the cautious reassessment of reported Sino-Japanese rapprochement moves.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1304 Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of April, 1935 (Report No. 103)
